newsitem.title: JAPAN: N.Korea's domestic media mum on defection.
newsitem.headline: N.Korea's domestic media mum on defection.

text.p: North Korea's domestic media on Sunday maintained their silence on last week's defection of a senior adviser to Pyongyang leader Kim Jong-il, media monitors in Japan said.

"All North Korean newspapers, radio and television to which North Korean citizens have an access have not reported anything on the defection of secretary Hwang Jang-yop," said Shinya Kato at Tokyo-based Radiopress news service, which monitors North Korean broadcasts.
"North Korean people have not been informed of Hwang's defection," he said.

The North's official Korean Central News Agency (KCNA), whose services are available only to foreign subscribers, on Wednesday carried the Pyongyang Foreign Ministry's angry response to Seoul's announcement on Hwang's defection.
The agency has been silent on the matter since then and the North's page on the Internet has also not mentioned it.
In the dispatch, the North Korean ministry said Hwang, now in South Korea's embassy in Beijing, must have been kidnapped.

"The South Korean authorities are spreading the rumour that Hwang Jang-yop, secretary of the central committee of the Workers' Party of Korea, asked for 'asylum' at their 'embassy' in Beijing today (Wednesday) on his way back from Tokyo. This is inconceivable and impossible," it said.
